items.question: Broker-stops design review pt1 (lifecycle)
items.advice: Verdict unknown: only design text seen, code not reviewed. Possible blockers to test: ratchet cancel-then-place race (don't place if cancel says already filled), duplicate tps- orders (deterministic client_order_id), unprotected window between cancel and re-place, atomic ledger …
items.why: CEO 11/17: adopted as tests. Fake-broker tests for all 4 points added and code hardened (deterministic client ids + write-ahead intent, atomic replace, final-status check, atomic state saves); broker stops stay OFF; code queued for Claude line-by-line review (not sent)

items.question: Broker-stops design review pt2 (stop width)
items.advice: Confirmed, width reasonable, no blocking gap proven. Test: already-below-stop reject must not retry forever, stale ATR rule, halts/splits, gap-through-stop loss. Backtest stopped-out trades not yet run.
items.why: CEO 11/17: edge-case tests added (stop above market: no retry loop + alert; stale ATR floor; halt; split freeze; gap fill booked at actual price); width unchanged; stops stay OFF

items.question: Mirror sync / reset paper account
items.advice: Yes reset to ~$17.5k (record old stats first); yes margin 1x and shorting off before seed (test T+1 settlement); order: reset+config, then seed, mirror on with stops OFF for one clean reconcile session, then enable stops; exclude CORE from qty alerts.
items.why: CEO 11/17: margin 1x + shorting off done on the paper account (stats saved first); reset to ~$17.5k NOT done: CEO option A keeps the $100k paper account (accepted difference, ledger drives all decisions); reconcile skips CORE QQQ; mirror ON 11/17 evening with broker stops OFF …

items.question: Open: other improvement ideas
items.advice: Ranked: 1 finish SPY alpha gate; 2 stop nightly tuning on same 126-session window, keep untouched holdout; 3 always-on host for tick gaps; 4 calibrate slippage/late-fill with mirror fills and compare 8% live vs 48% lab exposure; 5 point-in-time universe.
items.why: CEO 11/17: ideas 1-2 adopted (gate bar KEPT at t>=2.5, not lowered to 2; alpha net of costs incl. late-fill; sealed holdout from 2026-11-18; rolling monthly tuning window; retune at most monthly enforced in code). Idea 3 under way via the desktop shadow engine. Ideas 4-5 later

batches.title: Code and safety review, plus last week's lag (the code review was a one-time extra Ryan approved)

items.question: Review the trading engine's code for order, sizing and exit bugs.
items.advice: The QQQ position could trade on stale prices after the computer froze, and a crash could repeat a buy.
items.why: We added a stale-price guard, made catch-up after a freeze safer, and save the books after every trade.
items.performance: Live since Nov 13. It would have blocked all 4 late QQQ trades we checked.

items.question: Review safety: secrets, the public link, stale data, pauses and auto-tuning.
items.advice: Check the old public link's protection, act on freezes instead of just logging them, and require auto-tuning to be explicitly off.
items.why: The engine now refuses to start unless auto-tuning is clearly off. The old public link was later turned off.
items.performance: In place since Nov 13; no issues since.

items.question: What's missing before we could ever use real money?
items.advice: Big gaps: real order handling and matching against the broker, stops held at the broker, and a master kill switch.
items.why: Added to our real-money checklist. Not built yet, since we're staying on paper.
items.performance: Being worked on step by step. The always-on desktop engine is part of it.

items.question: Is our explanation of last week's lag behind SPY right?
items.advice: The numbers add up. The QQQ position held only about 55% of the book, and the weekly start point was off. One week can't judge the rule.
items.why: Weekly reports now split the gap with SPY by cause and start from Friday's close.
items.performance: In use from this week's (Nov 16) numbers.

items.question: Is next week's plan right, and are we at risk of over-fitting?
items.advice: Fix the weekly start point first, then measure late-fill costs, then decide the QQQ rule, then build the hiring test. Don't add new variants.
items.performance: Done. Late fills cost only about $8 net since Oct 10, mostly luck. The hiring test is built.

batches.title: Test plans before the Saturday lab, and the bot hiring test

items.question: Is our test plan for choosing the QQQ position's rule fair?
items.advice: The plan is fair and doesn't peek at the future. Add a few extra reports so the result is easier to trust.
items.why: We added the extra reports before the test ran and left the pass bar unchanged.
items.performance: The Saturday test ran cleanly. One rule passed: check QQQ against its 200-day average at each month-end and size for 20% volatility. Since 2000 it beat plain SPY by about 1.5 points a year with a much smaller worst drop.

items.question: Is our test of selling before earnings fair?
items.advice: Fair. Add a trade-by-trade report and make sure both versions skip new buys right before earnings.
items.why: We added the report and confirmed the setup before the test ran.
items.performance: Selling before earnings did not help (slightly worse), so we didn't adopt it.

items.question: How strict should the test be before a trading bot is allowed to trade?
items.advice: Make it strict: a strong statistical score (2.5+), tested at real sizes, with the last year held back and used only once.
items.why: We wrote this into the hiring test and fixed a bot whose results changed between reruns first.
items.performance: That bot (Trek) now gives the same result every rerun.

items.question: Saturday lab result: which rule should the QQQ position use, and should bots sell before earnings?
items.advice: Only the month-end QQQ rule passed. Caveats: its edge leans on 2000-2002, and the range of outcomes includes zero.
items.why: We switched the QQQ position to the month-end rule on Nov 14 and kept the old rule and plain SPY as paper comparisons. Selling before earnings: not adopted.
items.performance: Review in mid-May 2027, or sooner if it trails SPY by more than 5 points.

items.question: Applying the hiring test to our current bots: what happens to ones that fail?
items.advice: Don't keep bots trading on weaker evidence than we'd ask from a new hire.
items.why: Trek, Rota and Sunny all failed, so they were moved to paper-only on Nov 16. Each can come back after passing on 30+ new trades.
items.performance: Rota came closest (2.1-2.3 vs the 2.5 bar). Paper-only tracking started Nov 16.

items.question: Can Claude read our setup notes and send an answer back?
items.advice: Yes. Claude read the notes and replied without problems.
items.why: The Claude line was confirmed working, so we started using it for real questions.
